prompt.brief: Design a service that turns long URLs into compact links and resolves them with consistently low latency, even when traffic spikes.
successSignals: Separate the link-creation path from the read-heavy redirect path.
Choose a short-code strategy and explain collision and capacity behavior.
Keep analytics, abuse checks, and operational work away from redirect latency.
Cover aliases, expiration, deletion, privacy, and cache invalidation.

functional: Create a compact URL for a valid destination URL.
Redirect a short code to its current destination.
Support optional custom aliases and expiration dates.
Provide aggregate click analytics by time, referrer, device, and coarse location.
Let an authenticated owner update, disable, or delete a link.
nonFunctional: Keep p95 redirect latency below 50 ms for cached links.
Remain highly available because every redirect is user-facing.
Make private or unlisted codes difficult to enumerate.
Allow creation to be slower than redirects while remaining reliable and idempotent.
Treat analytics as eventually consistent and never block a redirect on it.
scaleAssumptions: 10 billion redirects per month with sharp viral peaks.
An average destination URL is about 120 bytes before metadata and indexes.
Read traffic is roughly 100 times heavier than write traffic.

metrics.label: Create traffic
metrics.description: Average write rate; quota and campaign bursts drive peak sizing.

metrics.label: Redirect traffic
metrics.description: Average reads; hot links can concentrate far more traffic on one code.

metrics.label: Code capacity
metrics.description: A seven-character Base62 namespace leaves ample room for growth.

metrics.label: Link storage
metrics.description: Redirect rows stay small; raw click events usually dominate storage.

entities.name: ShortLink
entities.notes: Authoritative link metadata and lifecycle state.

entities.name: ClickEvent
entities.notes: Privacy-scoped redirect event emitted off the hot path.

apis.contract: { destination, customAlias?, expiresAt?, idempotencyKey } -> { linkId, alias, status }
apis.notes: Validate destination, reserve a collision-free alias, and write link metadata.
Resolve from edge/cache with a database fallback and enforce status/expiry.

apis.contract: { destination?, expiresAt?, status?, expectedVersion } -> { alias, version }
apis.notes: Update authorized metadata and invalidate the alias projection.
Read asynchronous click aggregates with a known processing watermark.

dataFlow.title: Create a compact link
dataFlow.description: The service validates the destination and policy, allocates a collision-free alias, and commits metadata before returning it.

dataFlow.title: Resolve a redirect
dataFlow.description: Edge and link cache resolve the alias; a miss reads the link store, checks status and expiry, then returns the redirect with bounded latency.

dataFlow.title: Emit click telemetry
dataFlow.description: The redirect path appends a privacy-scoped click event asynchronously or through a buffered queue without waiting for analytics.

dataFlow.title: Aggregate analytics
dataFlow.description: Workers deduplicate events, build time buckets, and expose a processing watermark for dashboards.

dataFlow.title: Expire, update, or delete
dataFlow.description: Lifecycle workers and owner commands invalidate caches, tombstone aliases, and retain only policy-approved analytics and audit data.

architecture.title: URL Shortener reference architecture
architecture.summary: A cache-first redirect path keeps hot links fast while link creation and analytics remain reliable and asynchronous.

layers.label: Serving layer
layers.description: Clients, edge routing, and synchronous services that handle link creation and redirects.

layers.label: State layer
layers.description: Fast redirect lookups backed by authoritative link metadata.

layers.label: Async analytics layer
layers.description: Click events leave the redirect path and are processed into queryable aggregates.

keyPaths.label: Redirect path
keyPaths.description: Edge → gateway → redirect service → cache, with a database fallback on a miss.

keyPaths.label: Analytics path
keyPaths.description: The redirect service emits a click event without waiting for aggregation.

components.label: Service clients
components.description: Browsers, mobile apps, and crawlers that create or follow links.

components.label: Edge / CDN
components.description: Terminates connections and serves hot redirects close to users.

components.label: Service gateway
components.description: Validates requests, applies quotas, and routes create/read traffic.

components.label: Link Service
components.description: Creates codes, resolves redirects, and emits click events.

components.label: ID Generator
components.description: Reserves unique short codes for new links.

components.label: Redirect Cache
components.description: Caches code-to-destination mappings for the read-heavy path.

components.label: Link Store
components.description: Authoritative store for links, aliases, ownership, and expiry.

components.label: Click Event Queue
components.description: Buffers redirect analytics so the user-facing path stays fast.

components.label: Analytics Worker
components.description: Normalizes click events and rolls them into time buckets.

components.label: Analytics Store
components.description: Serves dashboards without scanning raw click events.

components.label: Monitoring
components.description: Tracks redirect latency, cache health, abuse signals, and queue lag.

connections.label: HTTPS
connections.description: Create or follow a short link.

connections.label: Route
connections.description: Forward misses and writes to the API layer.

connections.label: Create
connections.description: Reserve a unique code for a new link.

connections.label: Lookup
connections.description: Read the destination from the cache first.

connections.label: Miss
connections.description: Fall back to durable storage and refill the cache.

connections.label: Write
connections.description: Persist link metadata and alias reservations.

connections.label: Click event
connections.description: Publish analytics asynchronously before returning the redirect.

connections.label: Consume
connections.description: Process events independently from redirect traffic.

connections.label: Signals
connections.description: Emit latency, error, and abuse telemetry.

deepDives.title: Alias allocation and collision safety
points: For the low-latency URL shortener, redirect resolution must be fast but must never bypass link status, expiry, or owner policy.

Design for the failure case where hot aliases, cache staleness, destination abuse, and analytics bursts must not affect redirects or expose deleted links; keep retries, versions, and repair state explicit.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

deepDives.title: Redirect cache and invalidation
points: For the low-latency URL shortener, redirect resolution must be fast but must never bypass link status, expiry, or owner policy.
Keep this concern off unrelated request paths and partition it by the low-latency URL shortener access key.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

deepDives.title: Asynchronous click analytics
points: For the low-latency URL shortener, redirect resolution must be fast but must never bypass link status, expiry, or owner policy.
Keep this concern off unrelated request paths and partition it by the low-latency URL shortener access key.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

tradeoffs.title: Random IDs versus sequential aliases
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use collision-safe random or centrally allocated IDs with a uniqueness constraint and idempotency.
tradeoffs.caution: Sequential IDs are compact but reveal volume and become allocation hot spots without careful sharding.

tradeoffs.title: Long cache TTL versus revocation
tradeoffs.recommendation: Cache active links with TTL and targeted invalidation on update, delete, or expiry; always enforce a bounded expiry policy.
tradeoffs.caution: Long TTL improves hit rate but serves stale destinations after owner changes.

tradeoffs.title: Synchronous click logging versus redirect latency
tradeoffs.recommendation: Buffer or enqueue click events and keep redirect success independent of analytics availability.
tradeoffs.caution: Synchronous analytics adds tail latency and lets an analytics outage take down redirects.

commonMistakes: Generating aliases without a uniqueness/idempotency boundary.
Caching a redirect forever without expiry or invalidation.
Following redirects through a slow analytics transaction.
Allowing open redirects or malicious destinations without policy.
Treating analytics aggregates as exact source-of-truth events.

followUps.question: What if two requests choose the same custom alias?
followUps.answer: Reserve the alias with a conditional uniqueness write, return a conflict, and make retries with the same idempotency key return the original link.

followUps.question: How do you revoke a viral link quickly?
followUps.answer: Write a disabled/tombstone state, invalidate edge and regional caches, and recheck status on origin misses until TTLs expire.

followUps.question: How do you handle a click-event backlog?
followUps.answer: Keep redirects available, bound queue retention, scale analytics consumers, and report a delayed analytics watermark rather than blocking traffic.

rubric.description: The answer defines collision-safe aliases, low-latency cache reads, expiry/revocation, destination safety, and decoupled click analytics, scale, latency, durability, authorization, and failure behavior.
Entities and keys make the low-latency URL shortener state, versions, lifecycle, and derived projections explicit.
Partitioning, queues, backpressure, cache behavior, hot-key handling, and bounded work are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded behavior, observability, and auditability protect the primary contract.
The candidate can explain the low-latency URL shortener consistency boundary, asynchronous work, and operational limits.
